incidents.victim: US Critical Infrastructure (Water, Energy, Defense, Telecom)
incidents.vector: IRGC-linked operatives exploited internet-exposed industrial control systems and default credentials in water utility SCADA systems, as well as defense, energy, and telecom networks.
incidents.impact: More than 100 water utilities across 12 US states compromised; DOJ also charged IRGC hackers with breaching the Department of Labor, FERC, and UN organizations, and accessing the FBI Director’s personal email. A $10M reward has been posted for IRGC-CEC commander Amir Yaryab, who oversaw the CyberAv3ngers, DAA, and MASN groups responsible for these operations.

incidents.victim: Serbian Opposition, Activists, and Student Protesters
incidents.vector: Zero-click Pegasus spyware and NoviSpy mobile surveillance software deployed against targets’ devices; evidence from NoviSpy infections points to Serbian government authorities as the operator.
incidents.impact: At least 14 individuals targeted including a sitting Serbian MP, local officials, and peaceful student protesters; infections confirmed December 2025–January 2026, timed around Serbia’s March 2026 elections. Twenty-nine European Parliament members are now calling to freeze Serbia’s EU accession pending an investigation into the surveillance campaign.

incidents.vector: Type confusion vulnerability in Chrome’s V8 JavaScript engine (CVE-2026-85046) exploited in the wild to achieve arbitrary code execution in browser sessions.
incidents.impact: CISA added CVE-2026-85046 to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog confirming active exploitation against unpatched installations. All organizations should prioritize immediate updates to Chrome and Chromium-based browsers.

incidents.vector: Breach of a third-party shipping provider used by Trezor exposed customer order records from November 2019 through August 2021.
incidents.impact: An additional 67,000 US customers had names, email addresses, phone numbers, and shipping addresses exposed, widening a breach Trezor first disclosed in August 2026. Affected customers face elevated risk of targeted phishing and physical theft of hardware wallets.

incidents.victim: CrowdStrike, Kaspersky, and Avast Antivirus Users
incidents.vector: Public exploit code released targeting memory-parsing privilege escalation vulnerabilities in three widely deployed antivirus products; AV software’s elevated system privileges make these flaws immediately critical upon exploitation.
incidents.impact: The ‘Nightmare Eclipse’ group released three exploits: Falcon Flank (CrowdStrike), Hard Breacher (Kaspersky), and Pretty Prague (Avast). Organizations relying on these products for endpoint protection should apply vendor patches immediately and monitor for local privilege escalation activity.

incidents.vector: Two zero-days chained together — a max-severity pre-authentication SSRF (CVE-2026-83548) and a high-severity OS command injection (CVE-2026-83549) — enable unauthenticated remote code execution on internet-facing SMA-1000 appliances.
incidents.impact: Active exploitation confirmed in the wild; CISA added both CVEs to its KEV catalog. This is the fifth actively exploited SMA-1000 vulnerability since late 2025. Ransomware groups including INC and Akira have a demonstrated pattern of targeting SonicWall devices; organizations should patch immediately and hunt for signs of compromise.

incidents.victim: Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives (ATF)
incidents.vector: The Russian-speaking Qilin ransomware-as-a-service group breached the ATF’s CALEA (lawful intercept) system; method of initial access has not been publicly confirmed.
incidents.impact: 6.3 GB of sensitive law enforcement data briefly published, including names, phone numbers, and IP addresses of ATF investigation targets plus forensic data extracted from suspects’ mobile phones. ATF Director confirmed the breach investigation. The Trump administration’s recent authorization of private-sector cyber operators against criminal groups may lead to retaliation against Qilin.

incidents.victim: IDScan.net / Nexus Identity Verification Supply Chain
incidents.vector: Attackers exfiltrated driver’s license scan data from IDScan.net, a Louisiana-based identity verification provider used by retailers and hospitality companies, then sold 153 million records through a dark web service called Nexus.
incidents.impact: Over 153 million US and Canadian driver’s licenses — including those of government officials — are actively being sold on the dark web; the breach is estimated to have been ongoing for more than a year. Downstream customers of IDScan.net including Hertz, Target, FedEx, Planet13 dispensaries, and Caesars Entertainment are affected. FBI has launched a probe.

incidents.vector: ShinyHunters used voice phishing (vishing) to social-engineer a McKesson employee into surrendering Okta SSO credentials, then used those credentials to gain broad access to internal systems.
incidents.impact: ShinyHunters claims 284 million patient records stolen; if confirmed, this would rank among the largest healthcare data breaches in US history. Extortion demand is pending and McKesson is managing fallout. The attack follows the same vishing-plus-SSO playbook used against Jack Henry and other recent targets.

incidents.vector: ShinyHunters hackers used voice phishing to gain access to Jack Henry’s internal network and exfiltrate internal documents; same social engineering playbook used against McKesson.
incidents.impact: More than 7,200 bank customers notified of the breach; internal documents confirmed stolen. Jack Henry has refused to pay the ransom. The incident raises third-party risk concerns for any financial institution relying on Jack Henry’s banking platform.

incidents.victim: Open Source Software Ecosystem / Downstream Organizations
incidents.vector: TeamPCP deployed the Shai-Hulud worm to embed malicious code into hundreds of open-source software packages across multiple repositories and language ecosystems.
incidents.impact: Two alleged TeamPCP members (ages 21 and 23) arrested by Australian Federal Police in Western Australia; criminal charges pending. Organizations that consumed affected open-source packages may have implanted backdoors or exfiltrated data and should audit dependency provenance.

incidents.vector: ToxicPanda 2.0 banking trojan distributed via sideloaded Android applications; intercepts NFC payment data and one-time passwords to conduct unauthorized transactions from victim devices.
incidents.impact: Target list expanded from 16 to 349 financial institutions globally, dramatically widening exposure for NFC payment fraud. Victims face unauthorized transactions that may be difficult to reverse; financial institutions should assess whether mobile fraud controls cover NFC interception scenarios.

incidents.victim: Coder Platform Users / Terraform Infrastructure Developers
incidents.vector: Attackers compromised Coder’s Cloudflare infrastructure and served malicious Terraform module registry servers to developers building cloud-hosted AI application environments.
incidents.impact: Malicious Terraform modules were delivered for 14 hours on August 31, 2026. Organizations that pulled Terraform modules during that window should immediately audit their cloud environments for unauthorized resource creation, modified IAM policies, or exfiltrated secrets.

incidents.victim: US Federal Agencies, Senate, Hospitals, Telecoms, Financial Institutions
incidents.vector: Nanjing Xinjiuwei Network Technology (QTFY) operated QScan (a distributed vulnerability scanning platform) and QTRouter (a covert traffic relay through compromised IoT devices) as commercial cyber services sold to China’s Ministry of State Security and People’s Liberation Army; DOJ seized hard-coded command-and-control domains.
incidents.impact: Infrastructure used to target US federal agencies, the Senate, hospitals, telecoms, and financial institutions for nearly a decade has been disrupted. This is the third China state-backed botnet taken down by the US since December 2023; the QTFY database contained close to a decade of internet scanning data. Related botnet infrastructure has more than doubled in size following each prior disruption, signaling a persistent rebuild cycle.

incidents.vector: Attackers registered Lenovo ID accounts using email addresses of existing Dropbox users, bypassed Lenovo’s email verification, then used the verified Lenovo identity to pivot into and take over the corresponding Dropbox accounts.
incidents.impact: Nearly 5,000 Dropbox accounts accessed and data downloaded in August 2026. The attack exploited a verification gap in a third-party identity integration, highlighting risk in any SSO or federated identity arrangement that does not enforce re-verification on account linking.

incidents.victim: Thomson Reuters C-Track Court Case Management
incidents.vector: Unauthorized access to the C-Track online court case management platform maintained from March through June 2026; discovered June 30, 2026.
incidents.impact: Sealed court records and sensitive PII — Social Security numbers, driver’s license numbers, and medical information — exposed across 12+ US states, the US Virgin Islands, and Canada. The breach poses direct risks to sealed investigations, protected witnesses, and individuals with confidential case records.

incidents.vector: Hackers breached TVING’s systems in early June 2026 and exfiltrated a large user account database.
incidents.impact: Personal data of approximately 40 million users stolen, comprising more than 70 types of PII including names, email addresses, and phone numbers. Company executives issued a public apology and offered user compensation; TVING faces regulatory fines for delayed incident reporting.

incidents.victim: Mexican Government/Transport and Brazilian Financial Sector
incidents.vector: Two AI-assisted campaigns: living-off-the-land intrusions into Mexican transport and government networks using LLM-generated script naming and NextChat AI infrastructure (April–June 2026); and job-themed phishing against Brazilian financial targets delivering custom remote access tools and a Go-based SOCKS5 proxy built with AI assistance.
incidents.impact: Confirmed intrusions across Mexican government and transport organizations (CL-CRI-1131) and Brazilian financial institutions (CL-CRI-1163). AI-assisted tooling marks a capability shift for Latin American threat actors, enabling faster development of novel malware and evasion of signature-based detection. Both campaigns assessed as ongoing.
